subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: Should OpenClaw treat assistant-visible sandbox fix hints plus CLI-through-exec `openclaw config patch` as a protected config-mutation boundary, and which mutation paths should remain operator-approved only?
rationale: The current evidence shows partial guardrails and risky hints, but the exact auto-writer is unidentified and the correct boundary affects security posture, cron behavior, and user config persistence.

options.title: Security-boundary review and targeted hardening
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the config mutation boundary, then remove model-visible protected config assignments and add provenance or approval for automated writes.

options.title: Narrow error-copy hardening only
options.body: Treat the remaining risk as message hygiene and remove config assignments from assistant-visible sandbox errors without changing CLI-through-exec authority.

options.title: Wait for reporter artifacts first
options.body: Hold implementation until logs or a live repro identify the auto-writer that created the reported patch files.

recommendation.title: Security-boundary review and targeted hardening
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the config mutation boundary, then remove model-visible protected config assignments and add provenance or approval for automated writes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent main history carries the affected sandbox, gateway-tool, and memory-core surfaces, making this the best available routing candidate for the boundary decision.
